stem: What is the underlying cause of the increased pigmentation in a caf\acute{e} au lait macule?

options.text: A significantly higher total number of melanocytes compared to normal skin.
Increased metabolic activity of the existing melanocytes.
A localized thinning of the epidermis allowing underlying pigment to show through.
The migration of deep dermal pigment cells to the surface of the skin.

explanation: The pigment cells in these lesions are more active in producing pigment than those in the surrounding skin.
rationale: Think about whether the issue is the quantity of cells or how hard those cells are working.

optionExplanations.A: Biopsies show that the number of melanocytes is actually the same as in normal skin.
optionExplanations.B: The pigment cells in these lesions are more active in producing pigment than those in the surrounding skin.
optionExplanations.C: The lesion is defined by the activity of pigment-producing cells rather than the thickness of the skin layers.
optionExplanations.D: The source attributes the color to the activity of the melanocytes already present in that specific area.

source.hint: Think about whether the issue is the quantity of cells or how hard those cells are working.
